content.title: Tiara Bolden scores 23 in final game as OSU falls to Wisconsin
content.text: By James Crepea | The Oregonian/OregonLive CORVALLIS — Oregon State’s season came to a disappointing end, falling at home to a Wisconsin team that hadn’t won in nearly two months. Tiara Bolden had 23 points, six rebounds and four assists to keep the Beavers in it. But the senior from Eugene also got off to a slow start, had a costly turnover and left a shooter open late in a 62-58 loss to the No. 3 seed Badgers in the first round of the WBIT in front of 2,014 at Gill Coliseum Thursday night. “Tough loss for sure; you don’t want things to end before it has to,” Oregon State coach Scott Rueck said. “I loved the fight. The game separated right before the half, then we came out in the second half and made it a game.” Freshman center Dorja Zaja scored a career-high 18 points for Wisconsin (13-17), which won the battle in the paint 32-24 despite being known primarily as a three-point shooting team. The Badgers, who had not won since Jan. 21, advance to play at No. 2 seed Miami (18-14) on Sunday. “We’ve been resilient all year; we’ve been battling all year,” said guard Destiny Howell, who scored 13 points. “This is a program that’s trying to create a different culture in Wisconsin and trying to have a different narrative of what Wisconsin basketball will continue to be.” Rueck said there was “no shame” in the home loss to the 15th place in the Big Ten, which had just two road wins on the season — last coming on Jan. 1. “They were really imposing at the rim, disruptive defensively and then obviously hit timely shots,” Rueck said. “We got outplayed inside but they’ve been playing against a bigger — we’ve been playing against less size." Jenna Villa scored 11 points and Kennedie Shuler had nine points and six assists for Oregon State (23-12), which got within 57-56 with 2:51 to go but didn’t score again until the game was out of reach. Howell scored nine points in the first quarter to help Wisconsin go on an 11-0 run and take a 15-10 lead after the opening frame. “In the first quarter we gave her space, and I’m like, ‘guys, we’ve been watching her all week. Why are we off of her? She is so talented’” Rueck said. The Beavers were disjointed offensively during the first half, shooting just 32.1% from the field. Six turnovers led to seven points for the Badgers. Yet OSU managed to stay within 31-22 at halftime. Oregon State opened the third on a 15-5 run, with 10 points from Bolden, who gave the Beavers a 37-36 lead with 5:58 to go in the third. “I let the game come to me,” Bolden said. “In the first half I feel like I was a little shaken and the pressure I put on myself. After experiencing that and being able to take a deep breath and reset and show out. That’s what I did.” Latest Beavers news No. 9 Oregon State baseball defeats Lamar 2-0 in first shutout of 2026 Oregon State women’s basketball reserve guard to enter transfer portal Former Saint Mary’s, Cal Baptist assistant added to Justin Joyner’s coaching staff at Oregon State Zaja scored Wisconsin’s last seven points of the third to make it 49-43. Shuler was on the bench from the 7:48 mark of the fourth quarter until 1:04 remained and while the Beavers trimmed a deficit from nine to four in her absence, they also made several costly errors without their point guard and WCC defensive player of the year on the court. Bolden hit a pullup jumper to cut the gap to 57-52 with 4:30 left, then hit a three to get OSU within 57-56. A shot clock violation gave the Beavers the ball with a chance to regain the lead, but Bolden was stripped and Kyrah Daniels (11 points) hit a three to open Wisconsin’s lead back to 60-56. Bolden was blocked, then left Laci Steele open off an in-bounds pass with one second left on the shot clock. Steele hit the desperation jumper from the left corner and made it 62-56. “Coach Scott talks about defensive execution and I totally take fault for that,” Bolden said. “There’s some things we all could have done better as a team, especially for myself. However, that was a tough shot. I believe that I was there and I contested it well enough.” Bolden is one of at least four OSU players whose college careers come to an end. Shuler, Villa, Ally Schimel and Catarina Ferreira are all in line to return next season. But roster uncertainty is nothing new for OSU, which enters the new Pac-12 in need of at least an infusion of size inside. Meanwhile, the Badgers will play at least one more game. “I think in this day and age it’s so easy to hit the eject button,” Wisconsin coach Robin Pingeton said. “This group of young ladies hasn’t done that all year. When you go through adversity there’s so many life lessons in there, but it’s easy to grow weary and they haven’t done that.” Support our coverage of women's sports We're adding a reporter to cover the cultural and economic impacts of women's sports through a Report for America partnership.
